hero.title: Know Your Rights. Protect Your Community.
hero.description: Immigration enforcement and police are used to divide and intimidate the working class. Know your rights, prepare your family, and stand together so no one faces ICE or the courts alone. This is how we fight back.

kyr_home.disclaimer: Disclaimer: These materials are for information only, not legal advice. Always consult a trusted attorney or legal worker about your specific situation.

emergency.title: Emergency & Preparation
emergency.subtitle: I need to know my rights or prepare my family.

sections.rights_prep_title: Know Your Rights & Prepare Your Family
sections.rights_prep_intro: The most important tools you have are the right to remain silent and the right to not consent to searches. Memorize them. Teach them to your family. The guides below provide step-by-step instructions for what to do in common situations.

tactics.title: ICE Tactics

surveillance.title: Surveillance
surveillance.description: Follow you near your home or in public spaces

plain_clothes.title: Plain Clothes
plain_clothes.description: Wear plain clothes without identifying themselves

identity.title: Identity Confirmation
identity.description: Call out your name to confirm your identity

list: Follow you near your home or in public spaces.
Wear plain clothes without identifying themselves.
Call out your name to confirm your identity.

stopped.title: If stopped by ICE
stopped.silent: Stay silent. Do not state your name or answer questions.

if_yes.title: If they say YES:
steps: Walk away calmly if they let you.

if_no.title: If they say NO:
steps: SAY: "I will not answer questions. I want a lawyer."
Do not lie, show false documents, or run.

protect.title: Protect Yourself

record.title: Record
record.description: Record the encounter or ask someone to record. Anything you say can be used against you, so stick to repeating your rights.

anonymity.title: Stay Anonymous
anonymity.description: When requesting help, avoid saying your name. Give them a contact's name to send the video.

emergency_card.title: Emergency Card
emergency_card.description: Carry an emergency card with your lawyer's and family's contact information.

non_consent.title: Do Not Consent
non_consent.description: If searched without consent, say: "I do not consent to this search. I want a lawyer."

protect.search_script: "I do not consent to this search. I want a lawyer."
list: Record the encounter or ask someone to record. Remember that anything you say in that recording can be used against you, so stick to repeating your rights.
When requesting help, avoid saying your name. Give them a contact's name to send the video.
Carry an emergency card with your lawyer's and family's contact information.
If searched without consent: Say, "I do not consent to this search. I want a lawyer."

hero.description: Stay calm, know your rights, and protect yourself during a traffic stop.

always_pull_over.title: Always pull over
always_pull_over.content: Pull over when any law enforcement signals you to stop, even if you do not think you did anything wrong.
always_pull_over.recording_tip: Start recording. If alone, place the phone in a cup holder or pocket while recording continues.

warning.title: Warning
warning.content: ICE uses unmarked vehicles and may wear plain clothes or vests labeled “POLICE” without identifying themselves as immigration.

window.title: Your window
window.content: Roll down your window slightly when asked.

providing_info.title: Providing information

drivers.title: Drivers must provide:
list: Driver’s license.
Registration and proof of insurance.

passengers.title: Passengers
list: Passengers can usually decline requests for their name or ID.
In some situations, an officer can require identification.
Passengers may refuse to answer questions about their address, immigration status, or place of birth.

advice: Request officer identification before presenting any documents.
Do not lie or give false documents.

all_occupants.title: For all occupants:
list: Decline to discuss immigration status or criminal history.
all_occupants.say: Am I free to go? I choose to remain silent. I do not consent to a search.

exiting.title: Exiting the vehicle
exiting.content: Officer may order you to get out for “officer safety.” This order often precedes arrest.
exiting.warning: Officers may force removal if you delay.

search_limitations.title: Do not consent to a search
search_limitations.content: You can refuse consent to a search of:
list: Your body (beyond a pat-down).
The inside of your vehicle.
Glove compartment or trunk.
search_limitations.say: I do not consent to any searches.
search_limitations.repeat: Say this even if officers search anyway. Do not physically resist.

fingerprints.title: If ICE asks for fingerprints

if_requested.title: If ICE asks:
list: Ask: “Why am I being fingerprinted?”
Say: “I do not consent to fingerprinting.”

fingerprints.resistance: Do not physically resist. Verbal objection may protect your legal rights.

labels.timeline_aria: Steps to follow if ICE pulls you over

header.title: Protocol: ICE Interaction.
header.subtitle: Follow these steps immediately if approached at your home.

do_not_consent.title: Do not consent to a search
do_not_consent.say: I do not consent to entry.
do_not_consent.do_not: Open the door or step outside.
do_not_consent.instruction: Request badge numbers and names through the closed door.

ask_id.title: Ask for identification
list: Request badge numbers and names.
Record or write down this information.

no_warrant.title: If they have no court warrant, or only show a DHS or ICE warrant:
list: Say: “I exercise my right to remain silent.”
Say: “You cannot enter without my consent.”
Keep the door closed.

has_warrant.title: If they claim to have a warrant:
list: Request they slide it under the door or display it at a window.
Photograph the warrant.

check_items.title: Read the warrant carefully:
list: Look for the name of a federal or state court. A warrant issued only by DHS or ICE is not a court warrant.
An arrest warrant names a person. A search warrant identifies the place or person to be searched.
Read what the warrant allows. Check any deadline printed on it.

if_enters.title: If ICE enters your home
list: Record what happens, including any force, threats, lies, or searching beyond the warrant.
If you cannot film during the incident, record yourself describing what happened as soon as possible afterward.

invalid_warrant.title: If they do not show a court warrant that allows entry:
list: Say: “I do not consent to entry. I choose to remain silent.”
Keep the door closed.

if_enters.remember_script: I do not consent to any searches. I wish to remain silent. I want to speak with a lawyer.

kyr_ice_at_work.timeline_label: Steps to follow if ICE comes to your workplace

where_ice_can_go.title: Where ICE can go

public_areas.title: Public areas (no permission needed):
public_areas.description: Lobbies, dining rooms, and retail spaces. Entry alone does not give ICE authority to detain, search, or arrest anyone.

private_areas.title: Private areas (permission required):
private_areas.description: Without a court warrant, ICE needs permission from the owner or someone who controls the area to enter. California employers and their agents cannot voluntarily give that permission.

where_ice_can_go.warrant_note: In California, an employer must not voluntarily let ICE into a private or non-public area without a court warrant.

rights_at_work.title: Your rights at work
list: Remain silent.
Refuse consent to a search.
Stand together in the center of the room. Refuse to separate by immigration status. ICE uses this tactic to isolate individuals—protect each other.

hero.subtitle: Caution
hero.description: Understand your rights when ICE appears at your workplace. Know where they can and cannot go.

approaches.title: If ICE Approaches You
do_not_list: Run, resist, or lie about your identity
Sign any documents without an attorney
do_list: Stay calm and remember your rights
Ask if you are free to leave
approaches.say_this_text: "I wish to remain silent. I do not consent to a search. Am I free to go?"

employer.title: Employer Responsibilities
employer.intro: In California, your employer has rights and responsibilities during an ICE visit:

warrant.title: Ask for Warrant
warrant.desc: Can ask to see a court warrant

deny.title: Deny Access
deny.desc: Must not voluntarily allow entry to non-public areas without a court warrant

attorney.title: Call Attorney
attorney.desc: Can contact company lawyer before cooperating

notify.title: Notify Workers
notify.desc: Can inform employees of their rights

header.title: Documents to Keep
header.description: Know which documents to carry, when to show them, and how to protect your rights based on your immigration status.

safety.title: Document Safety
list: Make copies of everything. Keep backup copies with trusted family or friends.

legal_status.title: If You Have Legal Status
legal_status.includes_text: Green card, asylum, refugee status, valid student visa, or TPS.
carry_list: Your lawful resident card or immigration papers
show_list: Present these documents if law enforcement requests them

pending_status.title: If You Have Pending Status
pending_status.includes_text: Pending asylum application, open immigration court case, or immigration appeal.
carry_list: Copies of papers proving you applied for status or filed an appeal
show_list: Present these documents only if arrested

undocumented.title: If Undocumented or Expired
undocumented.carry_label: Carry proof of U.S. residence for 2+ years
carry_list: Documents showing your name, U.S. address, and date
undocumented.callout_text: These documents can prevent expedited removal without a hearing. Without proof of 2+ years residence, you can face deportation without seeing a judge.

legal.carry: Lawful resident card or immigration papers

remember.title: Remember
remember.text: "I wish to remain silent. I do not consent to any searches."
